texts: On day 100 of Year 1, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.
The mire-essence in the lantern held salt-bloom.
The nightmoths landed on the lantern.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash collected the silken threads from the lantern at dawn on day 101 of Year 1.
Coraline Ash carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the third cauldron on day 101 of Year 1.
Mire-essence formed in the third cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in a clay vessel.
Coraline Ash drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 101 of Year 1.

q1_issues.issue: "left silken threads on the lantern" gives the threads Patient, but depositing leaves them unaltered, so the change test yields Theme — the same passage correctly gives "collected the silken threads" a Theme.
The per-member distribution rule copies the same Patient mis-assignment into each moth's leave event.
The pre-nominal participle in "the stored mire-essence" (statement 96) yields no atom, though the participle-as-modifier rule licenses (Member sk_mire_essence_2 stored).

q2_gaps: An enumerative ordinal on an object ("the third cauldron") with no associated event and no stated "-est" dimension: Ordinal's <scale> slot has no licensed filler, and the parse improvises by putting the entity's own class (cauldron) there.

A day-of-year date ("day 100 / 101 of Year 1", no month): (Day n) is defined at day-of-month granularity and the seeded date-ordering rules key on year/month/day, so the two dated days are stated but not orderable as written.

Locative PPs stacked on a substance/medium NP ("boiled ... in sea-water in the third cauldron"): the stacking rule covers a second "in" on a place NP only, so the nesting is unrepresented and the parse emits two coordinate Location atoms.
review.notes: Bare mass objects are handled two ways in one passage — "mire-essence" gets a witness, "salt-bloom" stays a bare kind constant — defensible (only the first takes later definite anaphora) but inconsistent on its face. Otherwise clean: name-internal kind typing for Harbor Station / Cauldron Hall, silken_thread's material-adjective modifier genus vs. clay_vessel's suppressed noun modifier, (TimeAtMost ... evening) for "by evening", Location-on-event-only for the storing, and group event + per-member rule for the distributive moth predicates.

issues.reason: Thematic roles decides by one test — 'does the object itself change?' — and depositing threads on a lantern displaces them unaltered ('displacement stays displacement whatever is moved'), which is the Theme branch the same parse already uses for 'collected the silken threads'; even on an unclear reading the stated default is Theme, so (Patient sk_leave_1 sk_threads_1) asserts a change to the threads the text does not state.
The per-member rule reproduces the identical mis-assignment inside its conclusion, (Patient (sk_leave $x) sk_threads_1), so every derived member event carries the same unstated change claim.

The licensing half stands — a participle used as a modifier is an adjective ('a laminated worktop' -> (Member sk_worktop_1 laminated)), so (Member sk_mire_essence_2 stored) is available and the parse records the participle nowhere as a property — but the defect half does not: 'stored' here is anaphoric, its referent resolves correctly to sk_mire_essence_2, and the storing is already asserted at top level by s13_ev/s13_th on that very symbol, so the omission emits nothing false and drops no stated content.

gaps_confirmed: An enumerative ordinal on an object ('the third cauldron') with no associated event and no stated '-est' dimension: Ordinal's scale slot has no licensed filler, and the parse improvises with the entity's own class (cauldron) — acceptable improvisation here, since the atom is true and well-formed, but the slot is genuinely uncovered.

A day-of-year date ('day 100 / 101 of Year 1', no month): (Day n) is the day-of-month slot and the seeded date-ordering rules key on year/month/day, so the two dated days are recorded but not orderable as written.

A locative stacked on a bare-mass oblique object ('boiled ... in sea-water in the third cauldron'): the stacking rule is written for a second 'in <Place>' on a place NP, and the oblique-object rule keeps a bare mass as a constant that LocatedIn's entity slot may not take, so the sea-water-inside-the-cauldron nesting has no licensed carrier and both PPs flatten onto the event as coordinate Location atoms.
new_gaps: The causative/inchoative alternation across sentences ('The lantern burned mire-essence.' ... 'The mire-essence burned slowly.') has no licensed identity link — coreference covers entities and pronominal event anaphora only — so the two clauses mint sk_burn_1 and sk_burn_2 and the Manner adverb lands on an event with no stated connection to the lantern that was doing the burning.
adjudication.defect_summary: Statement 50's compliant form is (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_threads_1) — the threads are placed, not created, destroyed or altered — and statement 53's rule conclusion takes the same swap, (Theme (sk_leave $x) sk_threads_1), with everything else in both bundles unchanged.
adjudication.notes: Apart from the leave-role, the passage is handled closely to the instruction set: name-internal kind typing for Harbor Station / Cauldron Hall, silken_thread's material-adjective modifier genus against clay_vessel's suppressed noun modifier, (TimeAtMost sk_form_1 evening) for 'by evening', Location-on-the-event-only for the forming and the storing, and group event plus per-member rule for the distributive moth predicates. The split treatment of bare mass objects (a witness for mire-essence, a bare kind constant for salt-bloom) is licensed either way and is motivated here by which one takes later definite anaphora.
